Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..name: GlobalTheory.TateLimit.redChar
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Reduced character
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..reading: Reduce a ℤℓ-unit-valued character modulo ℓʳ by composing with the map on units induced by ℤℓ → ℤ/ℓʳ.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..definition:
def redChar {Γ : Type} [Group Γ] (ψ : Γ →* ℤ_[l]ˣ) (r : ℕ) : Γ →* (ZMod (l ^ r))ˣ :=
  (Units.map (PadicInt.toZModPow r : ℤ_[l] →+* ZMod (l ^ r)).toMonoidHom).comp ψ

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..name: GlobalTheory.TateLimit.zr
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..title: Finite Tate twist
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..reading: On the rank-one module ℤ/ℓʳ, an element of the Galois group unramified outside S acts by the reduction of χⁿ. The integral exponent n can be negative.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Proofs..definition:
abbrev zr (D : LData F Ω l) (n : ℤ) (r : ℕ) :
    Representation (ZMod (l ^ r)) (GS Ω (D.S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F)))) (ZMod (l ^ r)) :=
  charRep (redChar (D.chi ^ n) r)

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.name: GlobalTheory.Published.PoitouTateDuality
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.title: Global Poitou–Tate assertion
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.reading: For every prime ℓ, eligible number field F and positive r, each primitive ℓʳ-th root determines an admissible family of local invariant maps. At every finite S containing the primes above ℓ, for every compatible set of valuations, cyclotomic character modulo ℓʳ and finite discrete continuous coefficient module, the definition demands nine-term exactness, both Sha dualities and vanishing of cohomology in degrees at least three. At ℓ = 2 it requires F to be totally complex.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.definition:
def PoitouTateDuality : Prop :=
  ∀ (F Ω : Type) [Field F] [NumberField F] [Field Ω] [Algebra F Ω] [IsAlgClosure F Ω]
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (r : ℕ), (l ≠ 2 ∨ IsTotallyComplex F) → 0 < r →
  ∀ ζ : Ω, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ (l ^ r) →
  ∃ inv : InvFam F Ω l r, IsLocalInvariants ζ inv ∧
    ∀ (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F))), ContainsAbove S l →
    ∀ (Av : S → ValuationSubring Ω), (∀ v, IsPlaceOver (Av v) v.1) →
    ∀ (μ : GS Ω (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F))) →* (ZMod (l ^ r))ˣ)
      (hμ : μ.comp (toGS Ω _) = cycMod F Ω l r),
    ∀ (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (ZMod (l ^ r)) M] [Finite M] [TopologicalSpace M]
      [DiscreteTopology M]
      (ρ : Representation (ZMod (l ^ r)) (GS Ω (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F)))) M)
      (hρ : ContAction ρ),
      NineTermExact S Av μ (invAt S Av μ hμ inv) ρ hρ ∧ ShaDual S Av μ ρ ∧
        ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → Subsingleton (Hn ρ n)

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.name: GlobalTheory.Published.PoitouTate.NineTermExact
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.title: Poitou–Tate exact sequence
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.reading: There exist two linear connecting maps making the global-to-local Poitou–Tate sequence exact. Degree-zero localization is injective, each consecutive image is the next kernel, and the final degree-two trace is surjective. The trace maps use the specified local invariants and the cyclotomic twisted dual.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.definition:
def NineTermExact (hρ : ContAction ρ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (δ₁ : Module.Dual (ZMod (l ^ r)) (H2 (twDual μ ρ)) →ₗ[ZMod (l ^ r)] H1 ρ)
    (δ₂ : Module.Dual (ZMod (l ^ r)) (H1 (twDual μ ρ)) →ₗ[ZMod (l ^ r)] H2 ρ),
    Function.Injective (loc0 S Av ρ) ∧
    Function.Exact (loc0 S Av ρ) (tr0 S Av μ j ρ) ∧
    Function.Exact (tr0 S Av μ j ρ) δ₁ ∧
    Function.Exact δ₁ (loc1 S Av ρ) ∧
    Function.Exact (loc1 S Av ρ) (tr1 S Av μ j ρ hρ) ∧
    Function.Exact (tr1 S Av μ j ρ hρ) δ₂ ∧
    Function.Exact δ₂ (loc2 S Av ρ) ∧
    Function.Exact (loc2 S Av ρ) (tr2 S Av μ j ρ) ∧
    Function.Surjective (tr2 S Av μ j ρ)

Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.name: GlobalTheory.Published.PoitouTate.ShaDual
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.title: Finite-level Sha duality
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.reading: Both degree-one and degree-two localization kernels are finite in each dual coefficient pairing. Degree two is linearly equivalent over ℤ/ℓʳ to the module dual of degree one with the opposite twisted-dual coefficients. Equality of the two cardinalities is included in each direction.
Development.AbelianVarietyTheory.Publish.definition:
def ShaDual : Prop :=
  (Finite (Sha1 (twDual μ ρ) (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)) ∧
    Finite (Sha2 ρ (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)) ∧
    Nonempty (Sha2 ρ (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av) ≃ₗ[ZMod (l ^ r)]
      Module.Dual (ZMod (l ^ r)) (Sha1 (twDual μ ρ) (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av))) ∧
    Nat.card (Sha1 (twDual μ ρ) (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)) =
      Nat.card (Sha2 ρ (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av))) ∧
  (Finite (Sha1 ρ (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)) ∧
    Finite (Sha2 (twDual μ ρ) (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)) ∧
    Nonempty (Sha2 (twDual μ ρ) (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av) ≃ₗ[ZMod (l ^ r)]
      Module.Dual (ZMod (l ^ r)) (Sha1 ρ (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av))) ∧
    Nat.card (Sha1 ρ (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)) =
      Nat.card (Sha2 (twDual μ ρ) (locFam S Av) (continuous_locFam S Av)))

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.Descends
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Tower descent
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: For each positive natural twist e and each number-field layer of degree ℓᵐ, the length of its locally trivial degree-one cohomology equals the ℤℓ-length of the cokernel of the ℓᵐ-th power of the e-twisted action of γ, minus the identity, on the dual module over the full Galois group. Positivity is part of this particular predicate.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.GenBy
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Generator bound
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The module X admits a surjective ℤℓ-linear map from functions on Fin R with values in ℤℓ. The images of the coordinate vectors generate X. R is an upper bound on the number of generators, and can be zero.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def GenBy (R : ℕ) (X : Type) [AddCommGroup X] [Module ℤ_[l] X] : Prop :=
  ∃ π : (Fin R → ℤ_[l]) →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] X, Function.Surjective π

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.jZero
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Reference layer
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Take the natural-number logarithm of R to base ℓ and add three. This gives three at R = 0 and floor(log base ℓ of R) + 3 at R > 0. The window namespace makes the same choice.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev jZero (l R : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log l R + 3

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.vl
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Additive valuation
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Use the discrete valuation ring’s additive valuation on ℤℓ with values in the extended natural numbers. A uniformizer has value one, a unit has value zero, and zero has value infinity.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev vl (x : ℤ_[l]) : ℕ∞ := IsDiscreteValuationRing.addVal ℤ_[l] x

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.IsLevel
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic level
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The valuation of u − 1 equals the finite natural number c, with c ≥ 1 and c ≥ 2 when ℓ = 2. In particular u is a principal unit distinct from one. This normalization distinguishes the group 1 + 4ℤ₂ at the prime two.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def IsLevel (u : ℤ_[l]) (c : ℕ) : Prop := vl l (u - 1) = c ∧ 1 ≤ c ∧ (l = 2 → 2 ≤ c)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.cokLen
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cokernel length
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Divide the target X by the range f(X) and take its module length over ℤℓ. A non-finite-length quotient has value infinity. In particular finiteness requires its own argument.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def cokLen (f : Module.End ℤ_[l] X) : ℕ∞ := Module.length ℤ_[l] (X ⧸ LinearMap.range f)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.InPow
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Divisibility of the image
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: For every x there is a y in X with f(x) = ℓᵏy. The preimage y is allowed to depend on x. This condition still makes sense on modules with torsion and does not require a linear choice of y.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def InPow (k : ℕ) (f : Module.End ℤ_[l] X) : Prop := ∀ x : X, ∃ y : X, f x = (l : ℤ_[l]) ^ k • y

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.Unip
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Unipotence modulo ℓ
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Some natural power (γ − 1)ᴺ maps X into ℓX. At N = 0 the condition reads X = ℓX, in which case a positive exponent also works. Equivalently γ − 1 is nilpotent on X/ℓX.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def Unip (γ : Module.End ℤ_[l] X) : Prop := ∃ N : ℕ, InPow 1 ((γ - 1) ^ N)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.twLen
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Twisted cokernel length
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Multiply γ by uᵉ, raise the resulting endomorphism to the ℓᵐ-th power, and subtract the identity. Take the length of its cokernel over ℤℓ. Both e and m in this operator model are natural numbers, and the length may be infinite.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def twLen (γ : Module.End ℤ_[l] X) (u : ℤ_[l]) (e m : ℕ) : ℕ∞ := cokLen ((u ^ e • γ) ^ l ^ m - 1)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.LDataCardLeFinrank.shaInv
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Intrinsic Sha length
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Work in the absolute Galois group of F with its canonical algebraic closure and coefficients ℚℓ/ℤℓ acted on through κ⁻ᵉ. Inside H¹ intersect all kernels of restriction to decomposition groups above ℓ and to inertia groups away from ℓ, allowing every prolongation of a place. The ℤℓ-length of this absolute submodule is shaInv, valued in ℕ ∪ {∞}. The comparison with shaLen supplies its description using G_S and a chosen localization family.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def shaInv (F : Type) [Field F] [NumberField F] (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (e : ℤ) : ℕ∞ :=
  Module.length ℤ_[l] (ShaAbs (qzG F (AlgebraicClosure F) l e) (Above F l))

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.funRep
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Conjugation action on functions
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: A Galois element acts on M-valued functions on a normal subgroup by pullback under u ↦ g⁻¹ug. This gives a linear representation for the pointwise module structure.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def funRep (U : Subgroup (G F Ω)) [U.Normal] : Representation R (G F Ω) (U → M) where
  toFun g := LinearMap.funLeft R M (conjHom U g)
  map_one' := LinearMap.ext fun φ => funext fun u => congrArg φ (Subtype.ext (by simp [conjHom]))
  map_mul' g h := LinearMap.ext fun φ => funext fun u => congrArg φ (Subtype.ext (by simp [conjHom, mul_assoc]))

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.Fn
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic field
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Fₙ is the intermediate field obtained by adjoining to F the root set in Ω of X^(ℓⁿ) − 1.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def Fn (n : ℕ) : IntermediateField F Ω :=
  IntermediateField.adjoin F ((Polynomial.X ^ l ^ n - 1 : Polynomial F).rootSet Ω)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.instNumberFieldSubtypeMemIntermediateFieldFn
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Number field on a cyclotomic layer
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The ℓⁿ-th cyclotomic field Fₙ over a number field inherits a number-field structure from finite generation as a module over its base field.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: instance (n : ℕ) : NumberField (Fn F Ω l n) := NumberField.of_module_finite F _

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.Un
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic congruence subgroup
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Uₙ is the subgroup of the full Galois group on which the cyclotomic character reduces to one modulo ℓⁿ.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev Un (n : ℕ) : Subgroup (G F Ω) := levU l ⊤ n

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.Procyc
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Procyclic case
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The predicate Procyc is automatic at odd ℓ. At ℓ = 2 it requires the cyclotomic character reduced modulo four to be trivial on the whole Galois group.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def Procyc : Prop := l ≠ 2 ∨ ∀ g, cycR F Ω l 2 g = 1

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.Dinf
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic character module
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: D∞ is the ℤℓ-submodule of functions from U ∩ ker κ to ℚℓ/ℤℓ selected by XDual at N. Its elements are locally constant additive characters that vanish on every inertia subgroup intersected with the domain. They also vanish on its intersection with the decomposition subgroup of every valuation A for which A(N) < 1. At N = ℓ this imposes unramifiedness and complete splitting above ℓ in the dual Galois interpretation.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev Dinf (N : ℕ) (U : Subgroup (G F Ω)) : Submodule ℤ_[l] (cycU l U → QZ l) := XDual N (cycU l U) ℤ_[l] (QZ l)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Kum.Xinf
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Dual Iwasawa module
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: X∞ is the module of all ℤℓ-linear maps from D∞ to ℚℓ/ℤℓ. The formal construction uses the algebraic linear dual with this divisible target. The action of a Galois element on a functional uses the inverse action on its argument.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev Xinf (N : ℕ) (U : Subgroup (G F Ω)) : Type := Dinf l N U →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] QZ l

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.abelian₂.oneUnits
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Principal units of a local ring
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The one-units of a local ring are the units u for which u − 1 belongs to the maximal ideal. The source gives the subgroup laws explicitly.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def oneUnits : Subgroup Oˣ where
  carrier := {u | (u : O) - 1 ∈ maximalIdeal O}
  one_mem' := by simp
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := by
    have := (maximalIdeal O).add_mem (Ideal.mul_mem_right (b : O) _ ha) hb
    simpa [sub_mul] using this
  inv_mem' {a} ha := by
    have := (maximalIdeal O).neg_mem (Ideal.mul_mem_right ((a⁻¹ : Oˣ) : O) _ ha)
    simpa [sub_mul] using this

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.abelian₂.pt
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Difference of a principal unit from one
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: A one-unit u gives the point u − 1 in the maximal ideal, equipped with the membership proof carried by u.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def pt (u : oneUnits O) : maximalIdeal O := ⟨((u : Oˣ) : O) - 1, u.2⟩

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Base.galOf
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Pointwise fixing subgroup
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: In the Galois group of Ω over k, galOf(k,E,Ω) consists of the automorphisms fixing the embedded image of E pointwise.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def galOf : Subgroup (G k Ω) where
  carrier := {σ | ∀ x : E, σ (algebraMap E Ω x) = algebraMap E Ω x}
  one_mem' _ := rfl
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb x := by rw [AlgEquiv.mul_apply, hb, ha]
  inv_mem' {a} ha x := a.symm_apply_eq.2 (ha x).symm

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Base.galEmb
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Restriction of scalars on automorphisms
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Restriction of the scalar structure gives a homomorphism from automorphisms of Ω over E to automorphisms over k.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def galEmb : G E Ω →* G k Ω := AlgEquiv.restrictScalarsHom k

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Base.levU
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic level in U
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: levU(n) consists of g in U such that κ(g) ≡ 1 modulo ℓⁿ. Form the inverse image of the principal-unit subgroup and intersect it with U.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def levU (U : Subgroup (G k Ω)) (n : ℕ) : Subgroup (G k Ω) := U ⊓ (KStar.TotallyRealRoots.princ l n).comap (cycZ k Ω l)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Base.cycU
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic kernel in U
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The infinite cyclotomic kernel in U is the intersection of U and the kernel of the ℤℓ-valued cyclotomic character.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def cycU (U : Subgroup (G k Ω)) : Subgroup (G k Ω) := U ⊓ (cycZ k Ω l).ker

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Base.qExp
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Initial cyclotomic exponent
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The initial principal-unit exponent q is two for ℓ = 2 and one at every odd prime.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def qExp (l : ℕ) : ℕ := if l = 2 then 2 else 1

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Base.instNormalGCycU
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Normality of the cyclotomic kernel
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: If U is normal, so is its intersection with the kernel of the cyclotomic character. This instance supplies the normality needed for conjugation on functions.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: instance (U : Subgroup (G k Ω)) [U.Normal] : (cycU l U).Normal := by unfold cycU; infer_instance

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.HasMuQ
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Initial roots of unity
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The field contains a primitive fourth root of unity when ℓ = 2, or a primitive ℓ-th root when ℓ is odd.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def HasMuQ (l : ℕ) (L : Type) [Field L] : Prop := ∃ ζ : L, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ (if l = 2 then 4 else l)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.jZero
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Reference index in the window
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The window reference index is Nat.log ℓ R + 3. For R > 0 this is the base-ℓ logarithm of R rounded down, plus three. At R = 0 this gives three.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def jZero (l R : ℕ) : ℕ := Nat.log l R + 3

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.SecondBound
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Reference-layer growth bound
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Fix a positive natural twist e, any level-m number field L₁ and any field L₂ at the reference level j₀. For every algebraic closure of L₂ and choice of its local data D, the Sha length on L₁ is at most VLen(D,e) + R(m − j₀). Subtraction is in the natural numbers, so the extra contribution at levels below j₀ is zero.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def SecondBound (l R : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (L₀ : Type) [Field L₀] : Prop :=
  ∀ e : ℕ, 1 ≤ e → ∀ (m : ℕ) (L₁ : Type) [Field L₁] [NumberField L₁] [Algebra L₀ L₁], IsLayer l m L₀ L₁ →
    ∀ (L₂ : Type) [Field L₂] [NumberField L₂] [Algebra L₀ L₂], IsLayer l (jZero l R) L₀ L₂ →
      ∀ (Ω : Type) [Field Ω] [Algebra L₂ Ω] [IsAlgClosure L₂ Ω] (D : LData L₂ Ω l),
        shaInv L₁ l e ≤ VLen D e + ((R * (m - jZero l R) : ℕ) : ℕ∞)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.ABound
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Arithmetic tower bound
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: ABound is a conjunction. Its first part chooses an ultrametric normed field K over ℚℓ, naturals c and R′ ≤ R, R′ centres in K and a primitive ℓᶜ-th root in the base field. For every twist e ≥ 1, layer m and natural B, if every centre is at distance at least ℓ⁻ᴮ from e, the Sha length there is at most R′(max(m,j₀) + c + B). Its second part compares the length on every layer with VLen at j₀, with excess R times truncated m − j₀. The tower proof makes the particular choices K = ℚℓ and R′ = R, with all centres coming from ℤℓ.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def ABound (l R : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (L₀ : Type) [Field L₀] : Prop :=
  (∃ (K : Type) (_ : NormedField K) (_ : NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] K) (_ : IsUltrametricDist K) (c R' : ℕ) (s : Fin R' → K),
    R' ≤ R ∧ (∃ ζ : L₀, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ (l ^ c)) ∧
    ∀ e : ℕ, 1 ≤ e → ∀ (m : ℕ) (L₁ : Type) [Field L₁] [NumberField L₁] [Algebra L₀ L₁], IsLayer l m L₀ L₁ →
      ∀ B : ℕ, (∀ i, (l : ℝ) ^ (-(B : ℤ)) ≤ ‖s i - (e : K)‖) →
        shaInv L₁ l e ≤ ((R' * (max m (jZero l R) + c + B) : ℕ) : ℕ∞)) ∧
  SecondBound l R L₀

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.IsDesc
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Restriction compatibility of descent
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: A candidate descent map respects evaluation on the infinite cyclotomic kernel. If u′ in the ambient kernel is the image of u over L, the value there of the transported character attached to a Sha class equals the restricted class evaluated at u.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def IsDesc {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime] (D : LData L Ω l) (e : ℤ) (U : Subgroup (G k Ω)) [U.Normal]
    (Φ : Sha D e →ₗ[ℤ_[l]] ShaD l l U (galOf k L Ω) e) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Sha D e) (u : Uinf L Ω l) (u' : cycU l U), u'.1 = galEmb k L Ω u.1 → (Φ x).1.1 u' = resInf D e x.1 u

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.cokerLen
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Length of a module cokernel
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: For an endomorphism T of a module M over a commutative ring R, cokerLen is the extended length of the quotient M/T(M). Specializing R to ℤℓ gives the cokernel length in the operator model.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def cokerLen {R M : Type} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (T : Module.End R M) : ℕ∞ :=
  Module.length R (M ⧸ LinearMap.range T)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.IsGen
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic generator
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: γ belongs to U and the cyclotomic image of U lies in the topological closure of the integer powers of κ(γ). This asks for generation of the character image. The subgroup U itself can have a large kernel.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def IsGen (γ : G k Ω) : Prop :=
  γ ∈ U ∧ U.map (cycZ k Ω l) ≤ (Subgroup.zpowers (cycZ k Ω l γ)).topologicalClosure

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.dRep
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Action on cyclotomic characters
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The discrete action on D∞ is the restriction of the conjugation action on all ℚℓ/ℤℓ-valued functions to the stable submodule of allowed characters.

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.xRep
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Contragredient action
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: G acts on Homℤℓ(D∞,ℚℓ/ℤℓ) through its action on D∞ and the trivial action on the target. Thus g sends x to the functional φ ↦ x(g⁻¹φ).
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def xRep : Representation ℤ_[l] (G k Ω) (Xinf l N U) :=
  Representation.linHom (dRep l N U) (Representation.trivial ℤ_[l] (G k Ω) (QZ l))

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.dTw
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Negative twist of the discrete action
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Twist the conjugation action on D∞ by the character κ⁻ᵉ. The exponent is the negative of the integer parameter e.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def dTw (e : ℤ) : Representation ℤ_[l] (G k Ω) (Dinf l N U) := twist (dRep l N U) (cycZ k Ω l ^ (-e))

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.xTw
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Positive twist of the dual action
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: Twist the contragredient action on X∞ by κᵉ. Thus the operator attached to g is κ(g)ᵉ times the untwisted action of g, also for negative integer e.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def xTw (e : ℤ) : Representation ℤ_[l] (G k Ω) (Xinf l N U) := twist (xRep l N U) (cycZ k Ω l ^ e)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.ShaD
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Twisted invariants
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: ShaD consists of the characters in D∞ fixed by the e-twisted action of every element of V, with the action restricted along the subgroup inclusion.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
abbrev ShaD (e : ℤ) : Submodule ℤ_[l] (Dinf l N U) :=
  Representation.invariants ((dTw l N U e).comp V.subtype : Representation ℤ_[l] V (Dinf l N U))

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.cZero
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Exponent of the roots already in L
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: c₀ is the supremum in ℕ of the exponents c for which the base field contains a primitive ℓᶜ-th root. In its number-field application the set has a largest element and muQ characterizes it. The root of order one accounts for c = 0.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def cZero : ℕ := sSup {c : ℕ | ∃ ζ : L, IsPrimitiveRoot ζ (l ^ c)}

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.layU
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Subgroup of the m-th layer
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The subgroup of the m-th layer is the congruence subgroup of the full Galois group at c₀ + m. Thus the shift by the roots already in the base field precedes the layer index.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev layU (m : ℕ) : Subgroup (G L Ω) := Un L Ω l (cZero l L + m)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.layF
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Canonical tower field
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The canonical m-th layer is the field obtained by adjoining all ℓ^(c₀ + m)-th roots of unity to the base field in the chosen closure.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev layF (m : ℕ) : IntermediateField L Ω := Fn L Ω l (cZero l L + m)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.XP
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Dual module over the base field
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: XP is the algebraic dual of the character module for the full absolute Galois group, with the splitting parameter N = ℓ and the algebraic closure chosen canonically.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: abbrev XP : Type := XN l L (AlgebraicClosure L) l

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.Tower.IsTower
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Tower and generator hypothesis
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: The tower structure records four pieces of data about the base number field L and the prime ℓ. The field is totally complex, it has the prescribed initial root of unity, R ≥ 1, and a free ℤℓ-module on R generators surjects onto XP. The definition carries the generator bound directly.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
structure IsTower (R : ℕ) : Prop where
  complex : IsTotallyComplex L
  mu : HasMuQ l L
  pos : 1 ≤ R
  gen : GenLE ℤ_[l] (XP l L) R

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.IsLift
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Lift of a field automorphism
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: An automorphism σ of Ω lifts τ of F if it takes the embedded x to the embedded τ(x) for every x in F.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition: def IsLift (τ : F ≃+* F) (σ : Ω ≃+* Ω) : Prop := ∀ x, σ (algebraMap F Ω x) = algebraMap F Ω (τ x)

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.name: UpperTheory.V.IsLayer
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.title: Cyclotomic layer
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.reading: An extension L′/L is a level-j layer if it is cyclotomic of order ℓᵏ for some k and its degree is ℓʲ. This predicate applies to abstract fields with a given algebra map. The canonical intermediate-field model is supplied by a theorem.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Automo.definition:
def IsLayer (l j : ℕ) (L L' : Type) [Field L] [Field L'] [Algebra L L'] : Prop :=
  (∃ k : ℕ, IsCyclotomicExtension {l ^ k} L L') ∧ Module.finrank L L' = l ^ j

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.name: KStar.Selmer.H2
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.title: Matrix cokernel
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.reading: For a matrix Φ over R with finitely many columns, H2(Φ) in the matrix namespace is the quotient of the target coordinate module by the range of matrix multiplication on column vectors.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.definition:
abbrev H2 [Fintype n] (Φ : Matrix m n R) : Type _ :=
  (m → R) ⧸ LinearMap.range Φ.mulVecLin

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.name: KStar.TotallyRealRoots.redPow
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.title: Reduction on units
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.reading: Reduction modulo ℓᵃ takes ℤℓ-units to units of ℤ/ℓᵃ by the unit homomorphism induced by the residue map.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.definition:
noncomputable def redPow (a : ℕ) : ℤ_[l]ˣ →* (ZMod (l ^ a))ˣ :=
  Units.map (PadicInt.toZModPow a : ℤ_[l] →+* ZMod (l ^ a)).toMonoidHom

Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.name: KStar.TotallyRealRoots.princ
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.title: Principal units of level a
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.reading: The principal units of level a are the kernel of reduction on units modulo ℓᵃ. Equivalently ℓᵃ divides u − 1. At a = 0 the reduction has trivial target unit group.
Development.AutomorphicArithmetic.Cyclot.definition: noncomputable def princ (a : ℕ) : Subgroup ℤ_[l]ˣ := (redPow l a).ker

Formalism.ConjugateSelfDual.Statement:6:.name: Formalism.ConjugateSelfDual.G
Formalism.ConjugateSelfDual.Statement:6:.title: Galois group
Formalism.ConjugateSelfDual.Statement:6:.reading: G(F,Ω) is the group of F-algebra automorphisms of Ω. It is the absolute Galois group in this application because Ω is an algebraic closure of F.
Formalism.ConjugateSelfDual.Statement:6:.definition: abbrev G (F Ω : Type*) [Field F] [Field Ω] [Algebra F Ω] := Ω ≃ₐ[F] Ω

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalFinitenessK
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.title: Finiteness and cohomological dimension for local fields
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.reading: For a finite extension K of ℚℓ presented in the chosen ℓ-adic algebraic closure, and a finite discrete continuous ℤ/ℓʳ-representation of its absolute Galois group with r > 0, H⁰, H¹ and H² are finite and Hⁿ is trivial for n ≥ 3.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.definition:
def LocalFinitenessK : Prop := ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (K : IntermediateField ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l)),
  FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] K → ∀ (r : ℕ) (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (ZMod (l ^ r)) M]
  [Finite M] [TopologicalSpace M] [DiscreteTopology M]
  (rho : Representation (ZMod (l ^ r)) (GK l K) M), 0 < r → ContAction rho →
    Finite (H0 rho) ∧ Finite (H1 rho) ∧ Finite (H2 rho) ∧ ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → Subsingleton (Hn rho n)

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDualityK
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.title: Local Tate duality
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.reading: For the same finite local fields and finite discrete continuous modules at r > 0, H² of the cyclotomic coefficient has a linear identification with ℤ/ℓʳ. The degree (0,2), (1,1) in both evaluation orders, and (2,0) cup-product maps for the twisted dual are bijective.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LocalTateDual.definition:
def LocalTateDualityK : Prop := ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (K : IntermediateField ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l)),
  FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] K → ∀ (r : ℕ) (M : Type) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (ZMod (l ^ r)) M]
  [Finite M] [TopologicalSpace M] [DiscreteTopology M]
  (rho : Representation (ZMod (l ^ r)) (GK l K) M), 0 < r → ∀ hrho : ContAction rho,
    Nonempty (H2 (charRep (cycK l K r)) ≃ₗ[ZMod (l ^ r)] ZMod (l ^ r)) ∧
    Function.Bijective (cupH0H2TwistedDual (cycK l K r) rho (MonoidHom.id _)) ∧
    Function.Bijective (cupH1H1TwistedDual (cycK l K r) rho (MonoidHom.id _) (hrho.comp' continuous_id)) ∧
    Function.Bijective (cupH1H1TwistedDual (cycK l K r) rho (MonoidHom.id _) (hrho.comp' continuous_id)).flip ∧
    Function.Bijective (cup20 (cycK l K r) rho (MonoidHom.id _))

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:15:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.QZ
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:15:.title: Divisible torsion coefficients
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:15:.reading: QZ is ℚℓ modulo the ℤℓ-submodule given by the image of the inclusion ℤℓ → ℚℓ. It is the divisible ℓ-primary torsion group used as the target of characters and duals.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:15:.definition: def QZ : Type := ℚ_[l] ⧸ ZlSub l

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:17:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.instAddCommGroupQZ
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:17:.title: Quotient additive group
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:17:.reading: Addition on ℚℓ/ℤℓ is the additive commutative group operation inherited from the module quotient.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:17:.definition: instance : AddCommGroup (QZ l) := inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (ℚ_[l] ⧸ ZlSub l))

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:18:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.instModulePadicIntQZ
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:18:.title: Quotient scalar action
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:18:.reading: The ℤℓ-module structure on ℚℓ/ℤℓ is the quotient module structure induced by multiplication on ℚℓ.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:18:.definition: instance : Module ℤ_[l] (QZ l) := inferInstanceAs (Module ℤ_[l] (ℚ_[l] ⧸ ZlSub l))

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:19:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.instTopologicalSpaceQZ
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:19:.title: Discrete topology on torsion coefficients
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:19:.reading: Equip ℚℓ/ℤℓ with the discrete topology, denoted by bottom in Lean’s lattice of topologies.

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:20:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.instDiscreteTopologyQZ
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:20:.title: Discreteness
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:20:.reading: The selected topology on ℚℓ/ℤℓ is discrete by its definition.

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:21:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.instIsTopologicalAddGroupQZ
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:21:.title: Topological additive group
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:21:.reading: Addition and negation on ℚℓ/ℤℓ are continuous for its discrete topology. This makes it a topological additive group.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:21:.definition:
instance : IsTopologicalAddGroup (QZ l) where
  continuous_add := continuous_of_discreteTopology
  continuous_neg := continuous_of_discreteTopology

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:54:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.LData
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:54:.title: Global cohomological data
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:54:.reading: For a number field F, its closure Ω and a prime ℓ, the data specify a finite set S equal to the primes above ℓ, a valuation subring of Ω over each such prime and a character of the Galois group unramified outside S whose pullback is the full cyclotomic character. The choices enter the restriction maps in the Sha kernel.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:54:.definition:
structure LData where

  S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F))
  hS : (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F))) = Above F l

  A : S → ValuationSubring Ω
  hA : ∀ v, IsPlaceOver (A v) v.1

  chi : GS Ω (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F))) →* ℤ_[l]ˣ
  hchi : chi.comp (toGS Ω _) = cycZ F Ω l

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:67:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.qzTw
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:67:.title: Torsion coefficient twist
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:67:.reading: On ℚℓ/ℤℓ, an element g of the unramified-outside-S Galois group acts by multiplication by χ(g)⁻ᵉ. Here e is an integer, so inversion and the minus sign are part of the coefficient convention.

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:71:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.zlTw
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:71:.title: Integral coefficient twist
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:71:.reading: On ℤℓ, g acts through multiplication by χ(g)ⁿ with the integer exponent n. In VLen the chosen exponent n is e + 1.

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:75:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Sha
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:75:.title: Locally trivial degree-one classes
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:75:.reading: Sha(D,e) is the submodule of H¹(G_S,ℚℓ/ℤℓ(−e)) consisting of the classes whose restrictions vanish on every decomposition subgroup selected by D at primes above ℓ. In cochains one takes continuous crossed homomorphisms modulo coboundaries, then the intersection of the kernels of those restriction maps. This is degree-one locally trivial Galois cohomology.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:75:.definition:
def Sha (D : LData F Ω l) (e : ℤ) : Submodule ℤ_[l] (H1 (qzTw D e)) :=
  Sha1 (qzTw D e) (locFam D.S D.A) (continuous_locFam D.S D.A)

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:78:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.shaLen
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:78:.title: Degree-one Sha length
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:78:.reading: Take the ℤℓ-module length of Sha(D,e), the degree-one kernel of localization for the negative twist. The value is an extended natural number, so the notation includes infinite length.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:78:.definition: def shaLen (D : LData F Ω l) (e : ℤ) : ℕ∞ := Module.length ℤ_[l] (Sha D e)

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:80:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.VLen
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:80:.title: Integral degree-two length
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:80:.reading: VLen(D,e) is the ℤℓ-length of the entire group H²(G_S,ℤℓ(e + 1)). Here χ is the character in D, S is the set of primes above ℓ, and H² uses continuous two-cocycles modulo continuous coboundaries. The positive shift e + 1 is the dual twist paired with ℚℓ/ℤℓ(−e). The integral localization kernel sits inside H², and its inclusion yields the length inequality. VLen can have value infinity.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:80:.definition: def VLen (D : LData F Ω l) (e : ℤ) : ℕ∞ := Module.length ℤ_[l] (H2 (zlTw D (e + 1)))

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:82:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Sha2Zl
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:82:.title: Locally trivial degree-two classes
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:82:.reading: The integral degree-two Sha group is the submodule of H²(G_S,ℤℓ(e + 1)) whose restrictions to all decomposition groups chosen by D vanish.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:82:.definition:
def Sha2Zl (D : LData F Ω l) (e : ℤ) : Submodule ℤ_[l] (H2 (zlTw D (e + 1))) :=
  Sha2 (zlTw D (e + 1)) (locFam D.S D.A) (continuous_locFam D.S D.A)

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:92:.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.PTCase
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:92:.title: Admissible Poitou–Tate case
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:92:.reading: PTCase holds if ℓ differs from two or F has zero real places. Thus at two one needs a totally complex field.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:92:.definition:
def PTCase (F : Type) [Field F] [NumberField F] (l : ℕ) : Prop :=
  l ≠ 2 ∨ InfinitePlace.nrRealPlaces F = 0

Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:101.name: Formalism.GaloisCohomology.PTShaAt
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:101.title: Poitou–Tate length comparison
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:101.reading: Under the Poitou–Tate case condition, the ℤℓ-length of the integral degree-two localization kernel at twist e + 1 equals the degree-one Sha length for the torsion twist −e.
Formalism.GaloisCohomology.Statement:101.definition:
def PTShaAt (D : LData F Ω l) (e : ℤ) : Prop :=
  PTCase F l → Module.length ℤ_[l] (Sha2Zl D e) = shaLen D e

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.Dec
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.title: Decomposition group
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.reading: The decomposition group of a valuation subring A of Ω is its stabilizer in the automorphisms of Ω over F.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.definition: def Dec (A : ValuationSubring (Ω)) : Subgroup (G F Ω) := A.decompositionSubgroup F

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.cycZ
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.title: ℓ-adic cyclotomic character
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.reading: The ℓ-adic cyclotomic character κ of G(F,Ω) is the usual action on ℓ-power roots of unity. It is obtained by composing the action on Ω with the cyclotomic character valued in ℤℓ-units.

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.NS
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.title: Normal subgroup generated by inertia outside S
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.reading: N_S is the closed normal subgroup generated by inertia at all primes outside S, using all valuation subrings lying over those primes.

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.normal_NS
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.title: Normality of the inertia subgroup
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.reading: N_S is normal. It is defined as the topological closure of a normal closure, and the closure of a normal subgroup is normal.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.definition:
instance normal_NS : (NS Ω S).Normal := by
  unfold NS; exact Subgroup.is_normal_topologicalClosure _

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.GS
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.title: Galois group unramified outside S
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.reading: G_S is G(F,Ω)/N_S. Killing inertia outside S imposes the required finite-prime unramifiedness in the quotient.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Globa.definition: abbrev GS := G F Ω ⧸ NS Ω S

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.Z1
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: Continuous one-cocycles
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: The submodule of continuous one-cocycles consists of continuous functions satisfying f(gh) = f(g) + g f(h). Its module operations are pointwise.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition:
def Z1 : Submodule R (G → M) where
  carrier := {f | Continuous f ∧ ∀ g h, f (g * h) = f g + rho g (f h)}
  zero_mem' := ⟨continuous_const, fun g h => by simp⟩
  add_mem' := fun {f f'} hf hf' => ⟨hf.1.add hf'.1, fun g h => by
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, hf.2, hf'.2, map_add]; abel⟩
  smul_mem' c f hf := ⟨hf.1.const_smul c, fun g h => by
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply, hf.2, map_smul, smul_add]⟩

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.B1
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: One-coboundaries
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: One-coboundaries are the image of the degree-zero differential, taking a vector x to g ↦ g x − x.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition: def B1 : Submodule R (G → M) := LinearMap.range (d0 rho)

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.H1
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: Continuous first cohomology
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: H¹ is the quotient of continuous one-cocycles by the preimage of the one-coboundaries under the inclusion of cocycles in all functions.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition: abbrev H1 := Z1 rho ⧸ (B1 rho).comap (Z1 rho).subtype

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.Z2
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: Continuous two-cocycles
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: The submodule of continuous two-cocycles consists of continuous functions of two group elements satisfying g f(h,k) − f(gh,k) + f(g,hk) − f(g,h) = 0.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition:
def Z2 : Submodule R (G × G → M) where
  carrier := {f | Continuous f ∧
    ∀ g h k, rho g (f (h, k)) - f (g * h, k) + f (g, h * k) - f (g, h) = 0}
  zero_mem' := ⟨continuous_const, fun g h k => by simp⟩
  add_mem' := fun {f f'} hf hf' => ⟨hf.1.add hf'.1, fun g h k => by
    have e1 := hf.2 g h k; have e2 := hf'.2 g h k
    simp only [Pi.add_apply, map_add]
    calc _ = (rho g (f (h, k)) - f (g * h, k) + f (g, h * k) - f (g, h)) +
          (rho g (f' (h, k)) - f' (g * h, k) + f' (g, h * k) - f' (g, h)) := by abel
      _ = 0 := by rw [e1, e2, add_zero]⟩
  smul_mem' c f hf := ⟨hf.1.const_smul c, fun g h k => by
    have e := hf.2 g h k
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply, map_smul]
    rw [← smul_sub, ← smul_add, ← smul_sub, e, smul_zero]⟩

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.B2
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: Continuous two-coboundaries
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: Two-coboundaries are the images of continuous one-cochains under the inhomogeneous group-cohomology differential.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition: def B2 : Submodule R (G × G → M) := (contMaps R M G).map (d1 rho)

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.H2
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: Continuous second cohomology
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: H² is the quotient of the continuous two-cocycle submodule by the two-coboundaries, pulled back along the inclusion of cocycles in two-cochains.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition: abbrev H2 := Z2 rho ⧸ (B2 rho).comap (Z2 rho).subtype

ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.Hn
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.title: Continuous cohomology of degree n
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.reading: At degree n use the quotient of the n-cocycles by the n-coboundaries pulled back to the cocycle submodule. This supplies the vanishing predicates in degrees at least three.
ReciprocityTheory.GaloisValuations.Separ.definition: abbrev Hn (n : ℕ) := Zn rho n ⧸ (Bn rho n).comap (Zn rho n).subtype

ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCoh:132:.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.locFam
ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCoh:132:.title: Localization family
ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCoh:132:.reading: For each chosen prime v, the local family maps its decomposition group into G_S using its inclusion into the global Galois group and the unramified quotient.
ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCoh:132:.definition:
def locFam (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F)))
    (Av : S → ValuationSubring Ω) :
    ∀ v : S, Dec (F := F) (Av v) →* GS Ω (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 F))) :=
  fun v => locHom _ (Av v)

ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCohDefs:.name: ReciprocityTheory.Gal.charRep
ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCohDefs:.title: Rank-one character representation
ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCohDefs:.reading: A unit-valued character χ defines a rank-one representation on the coefficient ring by sending g to χ(g) times the identity linear endomorphism.
ReciprocityTheory.Hypotheses.GalCohDefs:.definition:
def charRep (χ : Γ →* Rˣ) : Representation R Γ R where
  toFun g := ((χ g : Rˣ) : R) • LinearMap.id
  map_one' := by ext; simp
  map_mul' g h := by ext; simp [mul_comm]
